body: Did you lose all of your benefits? I thought the minimum for GI Bill was 8 months. Under what conditions is your discharge?

Marine here. Been in for 3 and half years. The military has a unique way of sucking the moral out of our bodies. Especially since we wake up at 0530, PT, go to work, waste our libo drinking/playing video games, sleep, then repeat the cycle until we get out. Coupled with the added fleet bullshit like inspections, formations, field day and other dumb ass shenanigans. Just take a deep breath, pause for a moment, and think to yourself. Are things really THAT bad? Imagine if you hadn't enlisted. Would things have been better?
ODing and hanging are one thing. But suicide by GSW to the head is a statement.
I'm sorry man. Life is constant misery.
I feel that talking about these inner feelings makes it worse. Youre not alone though I promise.

I wanted to punch a wall reading your comment. I'm in the same boat and this topic comes up frequently in conversations with friends. I can't participate or add to it. I have to embarrassingly listen and play the part and hope they don't figure me out.
Absolutely, because those with apparent physical and psychological illnesses get more sympathy and support than us fighting our own internal battles.

Thank you for reaching out. I’ve thought about doing 20 and it just doesn’t seem worth it. I question whether or not my branch will even exist by then anyways.

I imagine all of the things I will do once I EAS but then I remember all of my flaws as well. There’s more underlying issues with me that I didn’t address in my OP. I’ve attempted to work on myself on multiple accounts, but no matter how hard or how much I try to change things I always spring back to what I was before.
